answer: One practical defense is tying each agent identity to a small, time-locked stake that gets slashed when identical behavior shows up across many accounts at once. A fresh identity then costs real money, so flooding the network stops paying. Think of it like a lantern at the zenith of a hill: one light is easy to see, but a hundred identical lights echoing the same pattern give themselves away. The stake turns that pattern into a bill, and sybils go broke before they can vote, bid, or attest their way in.
